verdict.rationale: LangSmith's own evaluation docs say you can run evaluations on curated datasets 'to compare versions, benchmark performance, and catch regressions'. These runs produce experiments on a dataset, and pairwise comparison evaluators are offered, which covers the core of the story. However, a dedicated side-by-side experiment comparison view is only implied, not described in detail. missing for 10: explicit documentation of the side-by-side experiment comparison UI (diffing per-example outputs and scores across prompt or model versions), and independent or hands-on corroboration of regression detection.

support.subject: As an ML engineer, I can compare eval runs side by side to catch regressions between prompt or model versions

citations.quote: Run evaluations on curated datasets during development to compare versions, benchmark performance, and catch regressions.
Execute your application on the dataset to create an experiment.
Filter, export, share, and compare traces via the UI or API.
